finding_key: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts::the cli oauth loopback callback has no `state`/csrf binding, so any local process or visited web page can inject an attacker's authorization code and silently log the cli into the attacker's account (pre-existing, out of diff)
evidence: Verified against packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts as supplied: the OAuth URL (`${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}`) carries no state, and the loopback handler in startCallbackServer resolves on the first GET /callback with any `code` param, with no state/Origin check; the code is then exchanged and saved via saveSession. This matches RFC 8252's login-CSRF concern for loopback redirects; the random port and 30s window reduce but don't eliminate exploitability. The claim correctly notes it is pre-existing and outside the diff. Possible server-side mitigations in rest-api.md are unverifiable here, but the CLI-side binding the claim says is missing is indeed missing.
